fixes.explanation: Hold on, friend, that one doesn't hold up. Their offerings are exactly where the LORD says they're robbing Him (Malachi 3:8). So that can't be what kept them from destruction. The reason is that He does not change (Malachi 3:6). I'd have loved to say they earned it, but the text says otherwise.

That's it, baker. After all those years, the LORD doesn't say, "Pack it up." He says, “Return to Me, and I will return to you…” (Malachi 3:7) The door is open. I spent years forgotten in the back of a junk drawer before an angel called me out, so that line hits me right in the apron.

Yes, baker! The text says, “But you ask, ‘How can we return?’” (Malachi 3:7) They ask how the return is done. I think that's a fair question, honestly. I've asked "how" at the oven door more times than I can count.

Feasts and Sabbaths are real things in Scripture, friend, but they aren't the answer here. When the people ask how they rob Him, the LORD says, “In tithes and offerings.” (Malachi 3:8) That's the exact spot He points to. If I stamped a Sabbath cookie when the order said tithes, I'd get a very confused customer and a very flat batch.

Right, baker. The LORD doesn't say a few. He says, “You are cursed with a curse, yet you—the whole nation—are still robbing Me.” (Malachi 3:9) He speaks of the whole nation, so it's much bigger than a handful of people.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, “…the vine in your field will not fail to produce fruit…” (Malachi 3:11) The vine is going to produce. That's a promise that doesn't come with an "if the weather feels like it."
